new_findings.rule: A store whose value is the bytes it overwrites (mem[a len n] = mem[a len n], or the same bytes of a word just stored there) is a no-op: drop it before decoding, so the word keeps its whole value (to).

new_findings.issue: These are the 5 remaining P2 calls. The two reads of mem[64] are separated only by stores at mem[64] + 32/52/55, which cannot write slot 64, yet they stay distinct variables, so the length '_268 - _269 + 36' does not fold to 36 and the call stays raw. The same call is decoded (positions(bytes32), args sha3(...)) where mem[64] was known.
new_findings.rule: A store at mem[64] + k with k >= 32 (or above the free-pointer floor) does not change mem[64]; two reads of mem[64] with only such stores between them are the same value.
